newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 8.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 8.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON- Worldwide advertising spending for 1996 is expected to be 7.7 percent ahead of 1995 in current prices, and 4.1 percent ahead on inflation-adjusted prices, Zenith Media, the media buying and planning arm of advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc, says.

MILAN - Spending by Italian ministries on advertising and publicity campaigns is seen rising this year but remains well below that spent in Britain and Germany, the Italian association of advertising agencies (Assap) says. The Italian state plans to invest between 450 billion lire ($263.5 million) and 500 billion lire in 1997 for public communication, Assap says.
ROCHESTER, New York - Bausch & Lomb says it has settled a lawsuit against competitor Pfizer Inc. Although admitting no wrongdoing, Pfizer agreed to take its Visine ads off the air.

LONDON - A television commercial for a Citroen car that used violent imagery and included a man metamorphosing into a devil should not have been aired when it was likely to be seen by young children, Britain's television watchdog the Independent Television Commission says.
WELLINGTON - DDB Needham, part of Omnicom Group Inc, says it has been appointed to handle all advertising and communication for New Zealand baking and foods company Allied Foods.
FRANKFURT - Television company ProSieben AG says a high profile TV advertising campaign paved the way for its stock market listing.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Business leaders and politicians from all over the world urge the European Union to take a soft-line toward cyberspace laws. In meetings between more than 40 government ministers and some 80 business leaders at the EU's Global Information Network conference, participants call for more private sector efforts to establish fair play on the Internet.

AMSTERDAM - French pay television group Canal Plus says its Dutch subsidiary is to pay 145 million guilders ($73.5 million) over the next five years for the rights to show live Dutch first-division football matches.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Justice Department has opened an antitrust investigation into the business of registering Internet addresses.

BUDAPEST - Irisz TV, a consortium led by U.S.-based Central Media Enterprises and the losing bidder for two new Hungarian commercial TV channels, says it will challenge the Hungarian radio and television body's decision to award the contract to Magyar RTL and MTM-SBS.

NEW DELHI - Indian Internet subscribers will grow to 1.5 million in three years from the present 80,000 as a result of the government's decision to open up Internet access, India's apex infotech association says.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. - Internet media company Yahoo! Inc. and Web bookseller Amazon.com say they reached an agreement under which Amazon.com will be the premier bookseller featured on Yahoo! The companies say they will offer users direct links related to Amazon.com book titles from every Yahoo! search result and book category page in a deal which combines the Web navigation guide with the largest online bookseller.

SINGAPORE - The Singapore government says it has renewed the publication licence of IS Magazine, after the publisher agreed to drop a personal advertisement column and adhere to guidelines on sexual content in local publications.

NEW YORK - Rupert Murdoch, chief executive of News Corp, says the company is exploring a "joint venture" with prospective partners for its HarperCollins unit, a decision that would cut News Corp's stake in the book publisher.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

NEW YORK - Bill Gates, chairman of Microsoft Corp, has held meetings with cable executives to pitch a new kind of television set-top box as part of its bid to build a franchise in consumers' living rooms, The Wall Street Journal says in its electronic edition.

CAPE TOWN - Rapidly rising prices are threatening South Africa's attraction to foreign film-makers, a spokesman for the industry says. Low prices are one of the main drawcards offered by South Africa, and Cape Town in particular, as a venue for shooting features and commercials.
LONDON - Vodafone Group Plc, Britain's biggest mobile phone company, is bringing its own name to the High Street in an attempt to cut costs, boost brand awareness and capture hesitant new customers.

NEW YORK - Rapid growth outside the U.S. has helped push Visa card volume to record levels. "In the rest of the world people are discovering that they would rather use a payment card than cash," says a Visa spokesman.
MUNICH - Carmaker BMW strongly denies a press report that it is considering selling the small car unit of its Rover Group to Chrysler Corp
DETROIT - Ford Motor Co announces a range of incentives for car buyers including a $1,500 rebate on the Taurus sedan, as part of a national programme.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

NEW YORK - If you're one of those who feels guilty or ashamed for loving those long hours you put in at your job, rejoice! Management experts say workaholism may actually be beneficial because hard workers tend to enjoy their jobs.

MOSCOW - It will be harder for Russian consumers to get their hands on cheap pirated videos as a group of Russian film distributors and television companies have formed an association to fight rampant video piracy. "Russia has taken virtually no steps against video piracy, and as a result the government loses $250 million a year in tax revenues," says a government official.

BANGALORE, India - Consumers around the world may soon be enjoying roses from India as the country's flower exporters push ahead in a quest to grab a big share of a global market worth billions of dollars, industry experts say.
